evidence: This paper uses an ensemble of Boosting, Random Forest, and Lasso to predict one-year mortality but does not examine or report variable importance. The analysis focuses solely on predicted mortality scores: "The trained algorithm was used to predict one-year survival for the test sample of one third of the population, and the distribution of healthcare expenditure over the year of follow-up by predicted mortality at one year was examined." Conclusions concern spending patterns at different mortality probability thresholds (e.g., "only 2.8% of total health care expenditure" at >50% predicted mortality) and comparisons between matched cohorts, not feature importance rankings or magnitudes.
